narrative:
Hello,

I'm a clinical pharmacist at a community health clinic in Ohio, writing about a patient of ours, a 59-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes who has been on metformin for a good while (I'd have to check the chart for the exact start date, but at least a couple of years).

She came in a few weeks back complaining of frequent cramping and tightening in her calves and sometimes her hands, mostly at night. It was bad enough that she wasn't sleeping well. Her electrolytes and renal function looked unremarkable, so we ran a broader panel, and her pyridoxine level came back low. No other obvious cause turned up. She does not take any other regular medications that I'm aware of.

We started her on a B6 supplement. Within about a month the cramping had stopped completely and a repeat level was back in the normal range. She continues on metformin at the same dose.

I wanted to pass this along in case it's useful for your records. Happy to answer questions.

Regards,
Dana Whitfield, PharmD

Dear colleagues,

Please find below a case forwarded from our local contact in Germany, received from a pharmacist, for your records.

The pharmacist reports on a 31-year-old male patient taking Sertraline Hcl 100 mg tablets, one tablet in the morning. No other medicines were named as suspect. The start date and indication were not given.

According to the pharmacist, the patient came to the pharmacy complaining of pain in the upper part of his belly, and later of more general stomach pain. He was then sent to hospital, where he was kept as an inpatient. The pharmacist understands that a cyst in his liver had bled. No further details on treatment, the length of stay, or whether Sertraline Hcl was stopped were provided. The current condition of the patient is not known to us.

The reporter has not been named in the forwarded message, and we have no hospital contact details. We will ask our local team to request follow-up information and will pass on anything we receive.

Kind regards,
Local Pharmacovigilance Office

narrative:
Dear Drug Safety team,

We are forwarding a spontaneous report received through our Japan affiliate from a pharmacist, as per our safety data exchange agreement.

The pharmacist describes a patient who is taking atorvastatin calcium. Age and sex were not provided to us. According to the pharmacist, the patient has developed a gradual decline in memory and thinking, including trouble recalling recent events and difficulty managing daily tasks that were previously routine. The pharmacist noticed this during dispensing visits and in conversations with the patient's family. Exact onset timing and duration of therapy were not given, only that the change appeared "over recent months".

No other suspect medications were reported. Dose, indication, medical history, and current status of the patient were not provided. We do not know whether atorvastatin calcium has been stopped or continued, and no test results were mentioned.

The reporter is a pharmacist based in Japan. We have asked our affiliate to seek follow-up and will forward anything further we receive.

Kind regards,
Pharmacovigilance Operations
Partner Safety Desk

Dear Drug Safety Team,

I am writing to report a case involving a 31-year-old woman under my care. She was started on sertraline 50 mg once daily on 21 July 2021 for a mixed anxiety and depressive disorder. Chlorpromazine 25 mg daily was begun the same day for the same indication. She had already been on oxazepam since about 9 July 2021, also for this condition.

During her pregnancy she developed a hypertensive complication, a toxaemia picture that we managed as pre-eclampsia. She was admitted to hospital for monitoring and treatment, and her stay was somewhat longer than we first anticipated. She has since recovered fully and the condition has resolved.

I cannot say which of the three medicines, if any, played a role, so I am listing all of them. I do not have the exact oxazepam dose to hand, but I can ask the patient's pharmacy if that would help.

Please let me know if you need further clinical details.

Kind regards,
Dr M. Laurent
General practitioner, France

narrative:
Hello,

I'm a pharmacist at a community hospital in the US, writing about a 56-year-old man who has been on Jantoven since about the 22nd of December 2021. He's had no other medications that I would consider suspect here.

He came to our ED a little over a week ago feeling washed out and short of breath on stairs. His labs showed his hemoglobin had dropped considerably compared with his last check at the anticoagulation clinic. He was admitted for monitoring and further workup, and his stay was extended by a couple of days while the team sorted out the cause and watched his counts. I don't have the final discharge details yet.

I can't say for certain how much Jantoven contributed, but given the timing I wanted to get this to you. Happy to pull more information from the chart if you need it. You can reach me at the pharmacy desk during weekday hours.

Kind regards,
Dana M., PharmD
Inpatient Pharmacy

narrative:
Hello,

I'm a community pharmacist writing to report a case involving one of my regular patients, a 74-year-old man who has been on Jantoven since mid-October 2020 for atrial fibrillation. He's been well managed on it for the most part and comes in monthly for refills.

At his last visit he mentioned feeling run down and winded climbing the stairs at home, which he hadn't noticed before. He also looked noticeably pale. He told me his primary care doctor ran bloodwork, and the results came back showing low iron stores with a low red cell count, which the doctor described as an iron deficiency anemia. He has been started on iron supplements. I don't have the actual lab values or any information on a workup for the cause.

He's still taking Jantoven as far as I know, and I'm not aware of any other new medications. I can try to get more details from his physician's office if that would help.

Best regards,
Dana Whitfield, PharmD
Riverside Community Pharmacy

Hello,

I am writing about my mother, who is 77. Since late November 2021 she has taken atorvastatin calcium 20 mg, one tablet every day. Her doctor gave it to her for high blood pressure. I thought that was strange because I believed this medicine was for cholesterol, but we trusted the doctor and she took it every day.

At her check-up a while ago, the blood test showed her liver was not normal. The doctor said her liver had been damaged. She had been feeling a bit tired, but we thought that was just her age. The doctor told us to go back for more tests. The latest results are better, and the liver numbers are coming down, though they are not fully normal yet.

I am sending this because I want to know whether the medicine could be connected to her liver problem. Please tell me if you need her medical records or anything else from us.

Thank you,
Her daughter

Hi, yeah, I'm calling about my wife, she's 34. Her doctor started her on metformin, I think it was about ten days ago, and I wanted to report something. Um, so a few days after she started taking it she broke out in this red, blotchy rash, mostly on her chest and arms, really itchy. And then yesterday her face got kind of puffy and flushed and she said she felt like she was having some kind of allergic reaction to it. She's never had allergies to anything that we know of. She took Benadryl and it settled down a bit, I think. Anyway, she stopped taking the metformin and hasn't had any since. We just want to make sure somebody knows about this. We also have a dog that barks nonstop, so sorry if you can hear that. My number is 555-0142, and you can call back anytime after five. Okay, thanks. Bye.

Dear Pharmacovigilance team,

I am writing to report the death of a patient of mine, a 74-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, who had been taking metformin 1500 mg once daily since 2020. She had no other treatment that I would consider relevant to this event.

About ten days ago she was brought to our emergency department by her daughter after a rapid decline at home. On arrival she was found to have a profound build-up of acid in the blood, which the team attributed to lactate accumulation. Despite intensive resuscitation efforts, she died the following day.

I have no other suspect medication to declare. Before this episode she was fairly independent and still tended her garden. I have not yet received the full hospital summary, but I can forward it once it arrives.

Please let me know if you need further information for your records.

Kind regards,

Dr. M. Lefèvre
General Practitioner, France

Hello,

I'm writing about my sertraline. I'm 50 and my GP started me on 50mg once a day back in August 2021. It was for a general low mood and feeling out of sorts, nothing very specific really, he said let's just try it.

I've noticed over the past few months that my fingernails have little dents or pinpricks across them, like someone has gone at them with a tiny pin. A couple of my toenails look a bit like that too. I've never had anything like this before, and I don't have any skin problems that I know of. I thought it was down to washing up without gloves at first, but I've been more careful and they haven't changed.

I'm still taking the sertraline every morning with breakfast. The nails are no better, and if anything the marks seem more noticeable. I just wanted this recorded in case it's connected. Please let me know if you need any further details from me.

Kind regards,
Janet P.
